answer: The system issues each new agent a zk‑nullifier linked to a marble‑sealed contract that mints one non‑transferable token after the applicant proves a unique biometric anchor via zero‑knowledge proof. The nullifier is recorded on a public island ledger, blocking any later enrolment that presents the same proof while keeping the identity hidden. An attacker must lock 10 ETH per fake identity and endure a 48‑hour challenge period, forfeiting the stake if a duplicate nullifier is detected, so each Sybil costs 10 ETH.
